turns.user_message: If a train leaves at 9:00 going 80 km/h and another leaves at 10:00 from the same station going 120 km/h, when does the second catch up?

steps.reasoning: We need to answer a math word problem. No need for tools. Compute relative speed: second train faster {{int:96:144}} vs {{int:64:96}} = {{int:32:48}} km/h relative. First train has a 1 hour head start, traveling {{int:64:96}} km in that hour. So distance gap {{int:64:96}} km. Time to close gap at {{int:32:48}} km/h = 80/40 = 2 hours. Starting from 10:00, after 2 hours => 12:00. So answer: at 12:00.
steps.text:
The first train gets a one‑hour head start, so by {{int:8:12}} am it is already {{int:64:96}} km ahead.

The second train travels {{int:96:144}} km/h while the first continues at {{int:64:96}} km/h, giving a relative speed of  

\({{int:96:144}} \text{km/h} - {{int:64:96}} \text{km/h} = {{int:32:48}} \text{km/h}\).

To close the {{int:64:96}} km gap:

\[
\text{time} = \frac{{{int:64:96}}\ \text{km}}{{{int:32:48}}\ \text{km/h}} = 2\ \text{hours}.
\]

Starting from its departure at 10:00 am, the second train catches up 2 hours later, i.e. at **12:00 pm**.
